bull.b: The five-year SK On relationship provides a defined path to larger-scale domestic battery activity, combining cell supply with potential pack purchases. Its duration and planned volume could support production expansion, customer access, and a stronger position in commercial, industrial, and utility storage.

NeoVolta’s systems address several customer needs rather than relying on a single application: backup power, solar utilization, and time-of-use management. This broader use-case coverage can support demand across residential and commercial customers as storage adoption develops.

Low leverage and sharply higher equity and assets improve NeoVolta’s near-term financial flexibility compared with the prior year. This stronger balance-sheet position may extend the company’s ability to fund operations and pursue expansion while it works to rebuild revenue.

bear.b: A decline to zero revenue indicates that commercialization has not yet produced a stable operating base, despite the prior year’s growth. Without a recurring sales stream, NeoVolta has limited ability to absorb fixed costs, validate demand, or fund expansion internally.

Continuing operating and net losses show that the current cost structure is far ahead of realized revenue. Prolonged losses can consume shareholder capital and make future growth dependent on additional financing unless NeoVolta restores sales scale and narrows its expense base.

Negative operating and free cash flow, combined with an accelerated FY2026 burn rate, leaves NeoVolta reliant on outside capital until operations improve. This dependence raises the importance of financing access and increases vulnerability if revenue recovery takes longer than expected.
